colophon: Thus ends the Śrī Bālā Rakṣā Stotram.

lines.1: O sole mother of all the worlds, granter of every desired fruit —
lines.2: protect me always from the snares of petty evils and from sins.
lines.3: O welfare of the world, O eye of the world, O mother of the world, O one who pervades the world —
lines.4: protect me from the webs of the world's evils, and take away every harm.
lines.5: The sin accumulated across a hundred other births, through the deeds of speech, mind, and body —
lines.6: destroy it, O queen of the gods; protect me with your compassion, without ceasing.
lines.7: Whatever wrong I have done across a thousand other births —
lines.8: ward it off and protect me, O refuge, O one who cherishes your devotees.
lines.9: All the sins committed by me, and those committed by my own people —
lines.10: destroy them today; protect me, O supreme deity.
lines.11: The misfortune that has come upon me from sins done knowingly or unknowingly —
lines.12: ward it off in an instant, O mother of the world, misfortune none else can turn away.
lines.13: The cessation of wrong action, the setting in motion of a virtuous life,
lines.14: and the contemplative union of my own self with the divine — grant me all this, O supreme goddess.
lines.15: Steady contemplation through the linking-worship of every enclosure-teaching of the Chakra,
lines.16: and the remembrance of my guru's feet as well — grant me this too, O ruler of the world.
lines.17: The unbroken enjoyment of the nectar-bliss of the Supreme Brahman,
lines.18: and a mind utterly unwavering — grant me both, O ruler of the world.
lines.19: That state worshipped by the gods from Sadashiva down to Brahma, and by the great sages —
lines.20: grant that to me, O supreme goddess.
lines.21: Swiftly warding off every obstacle raised by Indra and the other gods, by demons and by rakshasas —
lines.22: protect me, protect me, out of your compassion.
lines.23: Myself, those dear to me, the one who depends on me, my attendants,
lines.24: my benefactor, and my circle of kin — protect all of us fully, O queen of the gods.
lines.25: Whichever of my devotees acts kindly toward me to the best of their ability —
lines.26: protect that friend always; and even the one who hates me, turn into a friend.
lines.27: From danger of the body and beyond the body, from perils of every kind, or from fear that has no cause at all —
lines.28: protect me, O you who shatter the calamities of those who bow to you, O eye of the universe.
lines.29: Grant me a happiness made of everlasting bliss, stainless and unconditioned,
lines.30: and grant me unwavering devotion — O you who fulfill every desire.
lines.31: Whatever, by every means, still remains for me to do from here on —
lines.32: teach me all of it, O mother, you who delight in the welfare of every world.
lines.33: That discipline of the mind by which I may draw near to you —
lines.34: grant me that, and, out of compassion, O sovereign goddess, heal over the wound of desire in my heart.
lines.35: Lift me up with your compassion, O goddess — fallen into the ocean of worldly existence, afraid, without protector, my mind in despair —
lines.36: and set me at your lotus feet.
